negative_reviews.author: Maggie A.
negative_reviews.text: Firstly, store bought cheap dry ramen. My 8 year old was able to tell that.  Their ONLY non-spicy broth was made with pork and it  was very salty and so greasy  and I found a piece of PLASTIC in the soup. My daughter did not touch it , but it was the only non spicy one for some reason . Service slow; the waiter had to remind the kitchen to make our sushi. My cocktail was meant to have alcohol in it: it tasted like juice . They added the 10% service charge to the bill and then told me I could take it out; hate when people use cheap tactics to make you leave a tip for underwhelming food and basic service. Overall, disappointing for someone who likes Japanese food, will stick to my usual restaurant in China town for authentic food.

negative_reviews.author: Amélie Rauv
negative_reviews.text: Had to wait half an hour for someone to take our order. And when all of my friends go their food, it took mine an hour for it to come, everyone had finished theirs.

issues: BOH stock and food cost assessment carried out at site by Sophie Wang (HEC), report received 23/08/2026 - food stock minor, drinks stock and storage action needed, supplier and food cost critical.
JFC supply unreliable with no dependable delivery windows; Chicken Karaage and Chashu are both out of stock on normal spec and replacements are being sent group-wide.
Chicken Karaage replacement is 69.00 per case against 48.29 normal, 20.71 more per case (+43%) - a direct margin hit on every ramen using karaage.
Chashu replacement unit price looks cheaper but each case is only 6kg against normal spec, so more cases are needed to cover the same volume and the net cost may rise rather than fall.
Drinks storage disorganised - no zones, no FIFO, no par labels and poor visibility; drinks stock also sitting slightly above par.
Multiple gas cylinders on the floor with status unknown - in-use, reserve, empty and awaiting collection cannot be told apart.
Chemicals and cleaning over-ordered - roughly three to four months' supply of sponges and low-rotation chemicals on hand, tying up cash and storage space.
Food stock overstocked on coconut milk (Chaokoh) and bulk vacuum-packed shredded chilli, which carries an expiry risk if it is not rotated.

Site is already red on the dashboard for w/c 10/08 on sales -15.0% against target and food at 27.2%; the JFC replacement pricing is a live candidate cause of the food cost overrun and should be tested before the overrun is treated as site execution.
General manager position vacant, so the red light protocol's GM one-to-one step cannot run in its normal form.
actions: Reorganise drinks storage into zones with high-rotation stock at eye level and bulk lower down, and apply par labels and FIFO - Owner: Inka Cheung, Maged Greige (28/08/2026)
Audit and tag every gas cylinder as in-use, reserve, empty or awaiting collection - Owner: Inka Cheung, Maged Greige (28/08/2026)
Introduce a weekly front-of-house walk-through on drinks par and rotation - Owner: Inka Cheung (28/08/2026)
Cut ordering on sponges and low-rotation chemicals by 30 to 40% and move to a quarterly ordering cycle to free up cash and space - Owner: Procurement, Maged Greige (28/08/2026)
Review and tighten food par levels on coconut milk and shredded chilli, and enforce FIFO on the bulk shredded chilli to avoid expiry waste - Owner: Maged Greige, Sophie Wang (06/09/2026)
Track food cost daily and report the variance to the HEC until JFC restocks the normal protein spec - Owner: Sophie Wang, Maged Greige (28/08/2026)
